nodes.title: Conductor
nodes.purpose: Prepare a test case and report its current stage.
input: Problem: a SREGym test case, with its deployment, fault and evaluation rules.
Requests for the current stage and application details.
output: Current stage: diagnosis (find the cause) or mitigation (repair the failure).
Application description, relevant namespaces and enabled stages.
behavior: Deploy the application: the services under test, including any supporting databases.
Apply the fault: the change that causes the failure being tested.
Expose stage and application details through GET /status and GET /get_app.
Evaluate diagnosis with the case’s diagnosis oracle, which can use an LLM judge. Evaluate mitigation against the system/application state, then advance stages or restore the environment.

nodes.title: Stage adapter (setup)
nodes.purpose: Configure HolmesGPT for the current stage.
input: Current stage and application details from SREGym.
Conversation from the previous stage, when available.
output: Initial conversation built with the HolmesGPT prompt builder.
Configured HolmesGPT agent, started through ai.call(messages).
behavior: Load HolmesGPT toolsets tagged CORE or CLI and check their configuration and prerequisites. Configure the Bash policy and SREGym Prometheus/Jaeger MCP servers.
Use HolmesGPT’s prompt builder for the system and user messages. Add stage-permission guidance and the configured MCP toolset instructions to the system prompt.
Supply the user task: diagnosis or mitigation, application description, relevant namespaces and investigation scope.
Keep diagnosis read-only. Permit the selected Kubernetes write commands during mitigation under the Bash allow/deny rules.
Select the model and allow 100 agent iterations per stage. One iteration can request several tools. For Sonnet 5.5, omit the rejected temperature setting.
For the next stage, create an agent instance with new system instructions. Retain previous non-system messages and the shared tool-result directory.

sources.label: Toolset tag selection and prerequisite controls

nodes.title: ToolCallingLLM / DefaultLLM
nodes.purpose: Prepare conversation context and send the model request.
input: Stage instructions, earlier model replies and tool messages.
Available tool definitions and model settings.
output: Model request containing the current conversation and callable tools.
behavior: ToolCallingLLM manages the conversation and context budget. When compaction is needed, summarize older messages through the configured model client.
DefaultLLM sends a model request through LiteLLM and returns the response to ToolCallingLLM.
On the last allowed iteration, omit tools to request a final answer. Provider errors or cancellation can end the call earlier.

sources.label: ToolCallingLLM.call_stream: prepare context and call the model
Create the model client and agent loop

nodes.title: LLM
nodes.purpose: Choose tool calls or return a final answer.
input: Current conversation and available tool definitions.
output: Model reply, optionally containing several tool calls with names, arguments and call IDs.
Final answer when the reply contains no tool calls.
behavior: Use the conversation and tool descriptions to choose actions.
Supply query expressions or shell commands when the selected tool requires them.
Return tool calls for HolmesGPT to execute. Text alongside a tool call does not end the agent loop.

nodes.title: ToolCallingLLM / ToolExecutor
nodes.purpose: Send each requested call to its tool implementation.
input: Tool calls from one model reply, including names, arguments and call IDs.
output: Calls to the selected tool implementations.
Error results for invalid calls or denied actions.
behavior: Append the model reply and its requested calls to the conversation before execution.
Parse call arguments and resolve each name through ToolExecutor. Apply the SDK’s repeated-call check, parameter conversion and approval rules.
Execute the requested batch with up to 16 workers. Tool errors and denied actions become results for the model.
Keep each result associated with its call ID. Calls can finish in a different order from their requests.

nodes.title: YAMLTool
nodes.purpose: Run Kubernetes queries, resource counts and usage checks.
input: kubernetes_jq_query and kubernetes_count: resource kind, namespace, selectors and a jq expression (a JSON filter).
kubernetes_tabular_query: resource kind, namespace, selectors, columns and a row filter.
kubectl_top_pods and kubectl_top_nodes: no arguments.
get_prometheus_target: Prometheus service, namespace and target name.
output: Selected resource JSON, counts/previews, table rows, CPU/memory usage or target details.
Tool status, the executed command and any errors.
behavior: Render a fixed command or a parameterized Bash script from the YAML definition. Template variables supply any inferred parameters.
Run kubectl inside the agent container through SREGym’s Kubernetes access proxy.
For JSON queries and counts, discover resources and retrieve pages as needed. Run jq locally to select or count the results.
For table queries, request custom columns and filter rows locally.
For CPU/memory snapshots, run kubectl top against the Kubernetes Metrics API.
For target lookup, request Prometheus /api/v1/targets through the Kubernetes service proxy, then select the target locally. Access rules can reject the request.
Apply configured output summarization when a fast model is available and output exceeds its threshold.

sources.label: YAMLTool: parameter inference, template rendering and subprocess execution

nodes.title: RunBashCommand
input: bash: command text, suggested command prefixes and an optional timeout.
output: Command output, exit status or error.
Rejection if the command is not allowed.
behavior: Check the command against stage-specific allow and deny rules.
Reject commands that need approval because this deployment has no interactive approval callback.
Execute allowed commands in a Bash subprocess. Commands using kubectl follow the Kubernetes access proxy.
Run local pipeline steps, such as jq, inside the agent.
Run the command in a shell process group. At the timeout, terminate the group and finish collecting output within a bounded interval.

tool_definitions.name: bash
tool_definitions.route: RunBashCommand → permission checks → Bash; kubectl uses the Kubernetes access proxy

nodes.title: Python Tool classes
nodes.purpose: Run log, network, task, skill and image tools.
input: fetch_pod_logs: pod, namespace, time range, text filters and output limit.
fetch_webpage: URL. tcp_check: host, port and optional timeout.
TodoWrite: complete task list with IDs, descriptions and statuses.
fetch_skill: skill ID or name. read_image_file: image path in HolmesGPT’s result-storage directory.
output: Filtered pod logs, page text/Markdown or TCP connection results.
Formatted task lists, skill instructions, images and file information.
Failure or refusal information when a request cannot run.
behavior: PodLoggingTool delegates to KubernetesLogsToolset: retrieve current/previous container logs with parallel kubectl processes, then combine, filter and limit them locally.
FetchWebpage validates each URL and redirect, performs HTTP GET requests and converts HTML to Markdown.
TcpCheckTool checks the destination and probe budget, then opens a Python socket connection if allowed.
TodoWriteTool formats the supplied tasks and returns them to the conversation. It records the plan; other tool calls perform the work.
SkillsFetcher reads the requested skill from the configured catalog and returns its instructions. Remote skill lookup requires a configured data-access layer.
ReadImageFile reads an allowed image from HolmesGPT’s result-storage directory and returns image data for a vision-capable model.
Local processing runs inside the agent container. SDK destination rules and SREGym’s network policy determine which network requests can leave it.

tool_definitions.name: fetch_pod_logs
tool_definitions.route: PodLoggingTool → KubernetesLogsToolset → parallel kubectl logs → local filtering
tool_definitions.returns: Filtered container log text and errors

tool_definitions.name: TodoWrite
tool_definitions.route: TodoWriteTool → format the supplied task list in the agent conversation

tool_definitions.name: fetch_webpage
tool_definitions.route: FetchWebpage → validated HTTP GET → HTML-to-Markdown conversion

tool_definitions.name: tcp_check
tool_definitions.route: TcpCheckTool → destination/budget checks → Python socket connection

tool_definitions.name: read_image_file
tool_definitions.route: ReadImageFile → read an image in HolmesGPT result storage

nodes.title: RemoteMCPTool
nodes.purpose: Call tools provided by the SREGym tool servers.
input: Selected remote tool name and JSON arguments.
Replies from the configured tool server.
output: MCP requests to the Prometheus or Jaeger tool server.
Structured tool results containing returned content or errors.
behavior: Discover tool definitions through MCP (Model Context Protocol).
Send the selected name and arguments to the configured server over its SSE connection.
Serialize calls to the same server through a shared client lock.
Extract and combine returned content into a HolmesGPT tool result.

nodes.title: KubernetesAPIProxy
nodes.purpose: Forward allowed requests to the Kubernetes API.
input: kubectl requests using the agent’s configured Kubernetes credentials.
Kubernetes API replies.
output: Allowed API requests.
Filtered API replies or access errors.
behavior: Apply SREGym access rules to requests and returned resources.
Hide benchmark internals and selected sensitive resources.
Forward permitted requests and return access errors for blocked requests. Filtered mode blocks Kubernetes service-proxy requests, including target lookup.

sources.label: FilteringProxyHandler: validate, forward and filter API requests
Agent credentials and filtered network access

nodes.title: HTTP / TCP endpoints
nodes.purpose: Receive web requests and TCP connection checks.
input: HTTP GET requests from fetch_webpage.
Socket connection attempts from tcp_check.
output: HTTP content, redirects or failures.
TCP connection acceptance, refusal or timeout.
behavior: SREGym’s filtered network allows only the selected model provider and local SREGym services through an HTTP proxy. Arbitrary websites and direct outbound TCP probes are blocked.
The SDK also checks destinations. With the configured defaults, private/internal targets require explicit permission.
When access is permitted, FetchWebpage processes the HTTP response in the agent. TcpCheckTool reports the socket connection outcome.

sources.label: Allowed local services and provider endpoints
Isolated agent network and HTTP proxy settings

nodes.title: Prometheus MCP server
input: get_metrics: a metric query written in PromQL (Prometheus Query Language).
get_alerts: no arguments.
output: HTTP GET /api/v1/query with the supplied expression, or GET /api/v1/alerts.
Filtered metric or alert data as MCP text, or an error message.
behavior: Build the HTTP request with the supplied tool arguments.
Send it through the shared HTTP client, which retries selected HTTP failures.
Parse the JSON reply and filter records using SREGym visibility rules. Keep only firing alerts for get_alerts.
Return text through MCP. Prometheus evaluates the query expression.

tool_definitions.name: get_metrics
tool_definitions.route: RemoteMCPTool → SREGym Python handler → Prometheus GET /api/v1/query; Prometheus evaluates PromQL

tool_definitions.name: get_alerts
tool_definitions.route: RemoteMCPTool → SREGym Python handler → Prometheus GET /api/v1/alerts

nodes.title: Jaeger MCP server
input: get_operations: service name. get_services: no arguments.
get_traces: service name and lookback in minutes.
get_dependency_graph: lookback in minutes.
output: HTTP GET requests to /api/services, /api/operations, /api/traces or /api/dependencies.
Service names, operations, traces or dependencies as MCP text. Errors can return as text or a failed tool call.
behavior: Convert service and time arguments into HTTP query parameters.
Request Jaeger data through the shared HTTP client.
Convert returned JSON to text for the MCP reply.

tool_definitions.route: RemoteMCPTool → SREGym Python handler → Jaeger GET /api/services

tool_definitions.name: get_operations
tool_definitions.route: RemoteMCPTool → SREGym Python handler → Jaeger GET /api/operations with a service name

tool_definitions.name: get_traces
tool_definitions.route: RemoteMCPTool → SREGym Python handler → Jaeger GET /api/traces with service/time filters

tool_definitions.name: get_dependency_graph
tool_definitions.route: RemoteMCPTool → SREGym Python handler → Jaeger GET /api/dependencies with a time range

nodes.title: Kubernetes API server
nodes.purpose: Serve Kubernetes data and accept permitted resource changes.
input: Resource, pod-log, resource-metric and service-proxy requests forwarded by SREGym’s access proxy.
output: Resource JSON, pod log text, CPU/memory usage, operation status or errors.
Prometheus target JSON when service-proxy access is permitted.
behavior: Serve object reads and pod-log requests for the test application and its dependencies.
Serve resource-metric requests used by kubectl top through the Kubernetes Metrics API. Metrics Server supplies the recent CPU/memory measurements.
Accept permitted resource writes. Kubernetes controllers act on the requested state of the deployed application.
When access permits target lookup, forward it to Prometheus /api/v1/targets through the service proxy.

nodes.title: Prometheus
nodes.purpose: Evaluate metric queries and provide monitoring data.
input: Metric queries and alert requests from the SREGym tool server.
Target lookup requests through the Kubernetes service proxy.
output: Metric values, alerts or target details as JSON.
behavior: Evaluate PromQL against stored metric samples.
Serve alert data through /api/v1/alerts and collection-target details through /api/v1/targets.
Return JSON for the requesting tool server or local script to process.

nodes.title: Jaeger
input: HTTP requests with service names or time ranges from the Jaeger tool server.
output: Service names, operations, request traces or dependencies as JSON.
behavior: Search traces: records of request operations across the application’s services.
Return matching data to the tool server.
Store application traces, which are separate from the agent conversation saved as a trajectory.

nodes.title: ToolCallResult
nodes.purpose: Format each tool result for the conversation.
input: Tool results after command execution, local processing or MCP reply handling, including images.
Errors and permission rejections.
output: Conversation messages containing formatted tool results, call IDs and supported image content.
behavior: Format each result with its effective parameters, output, metadata and any error text. Include returned images when the model supports vision.
Append messages through ToolCallingLLM as calls finish. Start the next model turn after the batch finishes.
For oversized results, store text/images in the agent’s result directory and return file paths with a preview. Bash and read_image_file can retrieve needed content.
The formatted model message can differ from the client result data used by the trajectory exporter.

sources.label: ToolCallingLLM.call_stream: append tool messages and finish the batch

nodes.title: Stage adapter (submission)
input: Final nonempty answer returned by HolmesGPT.
output: POST /submit with the exact answer and stage.
SREGym submission receipt and, after evaluation, the next stage or end of the test case.
behavior: Send the answer without rewriting or evaluating it.
Wait for SREGym’s evaluation and stage transition. The diagnosis judge and mitigation checks belong to SREGym.
If another stage is enabled, configure HolmesGPT for it with the retained conversation.
Keep SREGym’s shared 1,800-second deadline across stages. Starting a new agent instance does not extend it.
While the agent runs, record HolmesGPT events/conversation separately from our added records. Recording preserves return values, adds I/O overhead and reports incomplete capture.
After collection, convert saved records to trajectory.json offline. Exported client tool results can differ from the formatted messages sent to the model.
